title: Mini-lane contingency and automatic descope triggers for cycle resilience
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: Problem: Mid-cycle scope bleed and unexpected task delays repeatedly force emergency reassignments and ad-hoc descoping, which leads to dropped metrics and stakeholder frustration. Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable mini-lane contingency ("mini-lane") model and automated descope triggers so PMs and Eng leads can (1) proactively reserve ~10-15% capacity per cycle across initiatives, (2) automate descoping recommendations when leading indicators hit thresholds, and (3) provide a clear runbook for activation and deactivation. Scope: - Define mini-lane allocation rules by role and initiative size. - Specify leading indicators (velocity delta, blocker-age, priority-sensitivity) and numeric thresholds that trigger a descope recommendation. - Implement a descope suggestion engine (dashboard + Slack alert) that lists candidate work items, estimated impact, and alternative mitigation (role shadowing, partial delivery). - Create a human-in-the-loop approval flow for final descopes with automated audit logs. - Ship an initial runbook and training session for PMs and Eng managers. Out of scope: Full automation of task deletion, cross-org budget reallocation, or automated hiring/shadow assignments in HR systems. Success metrics: - Reduction of mid-cycle unplanned descopes by 40% within two cycles of rollout. - Time-to-decision on descope recommendations under 24 hours (from alert to approved action). - >80% accuracy of descope suggestions as judged by PMs (feedback survey). Decision tradeoffs: - Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but delay action; aggressive thresholds increase churn. Proposal: start conservative, measure, then tighten thresholds. - Fully automatic descopes risk removing high-value edge cases; therefore keep human approval. Rollout plan: 1) Pilot on 3 cross-functional initiatives (Platform, Console, Dedicated) for 2 cycles. 2) Iterate thresholds, UI, and training. 3) Expand to org-wide. Operational notes: - Dashboard will surface per-initiative mini-lane usage, current triggers, and historical rescues. - Data sources: velocity from cycle planner, blocker/ticket age from Linear, CI flakiness and runtime SLO breaches from telemetry. - Security: audit trail will log approver, timestamp, and reason for all descopes. Links: PRD draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CR/Mini-Lane+Contingency+PRD, Design sketch in Drive: https://drive.google.com/mini-lane-design, initial GitHub prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pm-mini-lane/pull/12.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mini-lane allocation matrix documented and validated by 3 PMs and 2 Eng leads. 2) Dashboard wireframe implemented with live data for pilot initiatives. 3) Alerting pipeline sends descope suggestions to #pm-alerts and creates a Linear candidate list draft. 4) Runbook published and a 60-minute training session delivered to participating teams.
